For the Petitioners: Mr. Randhir Kumar
 For the State: Mr. Abhay Kr. Tiwari, A.P.P
 For O.P.No.2: Mr. D. K. Jaiswal
 -----
10/12.12.2024 The petitioners apprehending their arrest in connection with the case
registered under Sections 498A/307/34 Ipc and Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act have prayed
for grant of anticipatory bail.
2.  Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in this case and have not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.
The petitioner No.1 is the father-in-law and the petitioner No.2 is the mother-in-law of the informant/the O.P.No.2.
It is further submitted that the petitioners had neither demanded any dowry nor had tortured the informant for non-fulfilment of the same.

The allegation that on 29.10.2023 at about 12.15 P.M, the petitioners and co-accused Rakesh Kumar (the husband of the informant) set the informant on fire by pouring kerosene oil and throwing a match stick on her in the kitchen is completely false.

It is further submitted that Basant Thakur @ Rameshwar Thakur, who was called by the petitioner No.1 on 29.10.2023 to treat the informant, has stated during investigation that while he was treating the informant, he asked her the reason for sustaining the burn injury, then she replied that by mistake her 'Dupatta' caught fire from a heater.
However, on putting further question to her as to whether any one was involved in inflicting burn injury on her, she replied that no one else was involved in the said incident.
In fact, she got burnt by her mistake.
Even if it is assumed that the said witness is not a doctor, he can certainly be said to be an independent witness.

Moreover, there has been Dilip Modi @ Dilip Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178644453/
1 unexplained delay of three days in lodging of the present FIR.

sentences.text: Under the said circumstances, the petitioners may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
3. Learned A.P.P as well as learned counsel for the O.P.No.2 oppose the petitioners' prayer for anticipatory bail.
4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the materials available on record, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioners on anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the above named petitioners are directed to surrender before the concerned Court below within a period of three weeks.

If they surrender before the Court below within the aforesaid period, they shall be released on bail on furnishing bail-bond of Rs.20,000/- (twenty thousand only) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Bermo at Tenughat in connection with I.E.L. P.S. Case No. 19/2023 (G.R. No. 1251/2023), subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) Cr.P.C.
Satish/- (RAJESH SHANKAR, J)
